survey: A wall-mounted split air conditioner (indoor unit), seen at three-quarter view from below and to the left. A long white rounded body sits flush against the green striped wall, and its soft shadow on the wall shows it is mounted there. Blue-violet end caps close both sides; the right cap is the one you see, and its back edge meets the wall. A grey trim line runs across the front at about two-thirds height, with a small silver house emblem above it. On the underside is the air outlet: a horizontal louver flap hinged along the front lower edge, with vertical vane dividers behind it. Stylized cool-air beams come out of the outlet and fan down and forward. Simplifications like no visible pipes, no remote and no display are normal for the genre.
